text:
alex: FYI customer acme-inc opened an escalation — their EU-dedicated pool is intermittently routing to hosted us-west, huge p95 latency and unexpected hosted billing. sample request-id: 01FZ7X-9c.
maya: ugh, do we have pool id / pin metadata for that tenant?
alex: tenant: acme-inc, dedicated_pool: eu-dedicated-7, observed_target: hosted-usw-3. Reported around 2026-03-05T09:12Z.
jordan: can you paste the routing headers from a failing request? i want to see pin TTL and affinity cookie.
alex: here's a scrubbed header excerpt:
```
x-tenant: acme-inc
x-routing-target: eu-dedicated-7
x-pin-ttl: 0  # suspicious
x-affinity-hash: a1b2c3
x-fallback: hosted-usw-3
x-request-id: 01FZ7X-9c
```

lina: noted the pin-ttl = 0. that means the pin record expired in control plane and the router fell back. but should have preferred eu-hosted first, not us-west. looks like region selection heuristic took cost tier over region.
maya: any auth errors reported? customer said some 401s for a handful of requests.
alex: yes small fraction of 401s post-failover, likely token audience mismatch because hosted route uses different key set. sample error: "aud mismatch: expected: eu, got: us-west".
sre-bot: auto-alert: routing-ttl-zero detected for tenant acme-inc on eu-dedicated-7 at 2026-03-05T09:11:58Z. Escalation created: SR-9832.
support-engineer: repro attempt: hit eu-dedicated-7 with sustained QPS 200 for 5m, then evict one host -> routing should keep pin but backfill to local hosted eu. Instead requests observed to cross-region. attaching capture: /var/tmp/captures/01FZ7X-9c.log
jordan: possible bug candidate: when dedicated pool reports full and we trigger overflow, the routing policy uses region affinity list from tenant meta; if that list is empty it picks cheapest compatible region (cost tier) — i think cost-tier mapping for acme-inc maps us-west ahead of eu-hosted. Shouldn't happen when tenant has eu residency flag.
lina: agreed. can we confirm tenant residency flags and whether control plane had stale copy? alex can you fetch tenant metadata version?
alex: fetched metadata v: 42. control-plane log shows last update 2026-03-04T02:03Z. customer updated residency on 2026-03-04T12:30Z (after that log) — looks like a missed refresh window.
maya: so the root cause: stale residency in control plane + pin TTL expiry -> fallback routing chose wrong region -> cross-region lat and auth breaks -> hosted billing on us-west.
billing-bot: charge-notice: 0.7% of tenant requests billed to hosted-usw between 2026-03-05T09:12Z-09:20Z. estimated delta cost: $1,900.
support-engineer: workaround: force refresh tenant metadata and re-issue pin with explicit region affinity via admin API:
```
POST /admin/tenants/acme-inc/pin-refresh
body: {"pool":"eu-dedicated-7","affinity":["eu-hosted-1","eu-hosted-2"],"ttl":3600}
```
That re-routed traffic to eu-hosted fallback and eliminated 401s.
jordan: long term fixes: (1) ensure control-plane propagates residency updates immediately for tenants with dedicated pins, (2) change fallback policy to prefer same-region hosted pools if residency flag present, (3) add a pre-fallback auth-audience check to avoid 401s during cross-region fallback.
lina: also add probe: when pin-ttl == 0, run synchronous metadata refresh before choosing fallback. cheaper than full sync but avoids costy cross-region mistakes.
alex: will coordinate a hotfix patch and notify acct team for refund estimate. I'm opening a follow-up with infra: INF-4219.
support-engineer: steps to reproduce locally for oncall: 1) create tenant with dedicated pool and residency eu, 2) mark control-plane metadata stale, 3) set pin-ttl=0 on router, 4) simulate pool saturation so fallback triggers. capture headers and auth token diffs.
maya: do we need to throttle customer keys while we fix? acme-inc worried about user experience.
jordan: temporary rule: freeze cross-region fallback for tenants with residency flag for next 4 hours while we roll hotfix. can ops enact route-freeze?
alex: ops also requested: host ids, request sample and proof of TTL expiry. attached logs above. i'll ping infra and billing to start mitigation and refund convo.
sre-bot: note: route-freeze enacted for acme-inc at 2026-03-05T10:01Z (manual).
billing-bot: note: provisional refund queued, contact billing@redwood for approvals.
lina: adding this to postmortem bin. will create short action list and owner assignments.
alex: thanks. next update in #support in 30m or when hotfix lands. :thumbsup:
